question_stem: A nichrome resistance wire has length $150\text{ cm}$, cross-sectional area $2.45 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^2$ and resistivity $1.12 \times 10^{-6}\Omega\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Calculate, to three significant figures, the resistance of the wire.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem:
The nichrome wire forms part of a potentiometer circuit together with a cell of electromotive force (e.m.f.) $1.2\text{ V}$ and negligible internal resistance, as shown in Fig. 7.1.

{{figure:figure_7_1}}

Fig. 7.1 (not to scale)

The circuit is used to determine the e.m.f. of cell X.

The galvanometer is used in a null method to find the null point $64\text{ cm}$ from the left-hand end of the nichrome wire.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by a null method.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the e.m.f. of cell X.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The cell of e.m.f. $1.2\text{ V}$ is replaced by a new cell with the same e.m.f. but with an internal resistance that is **not** negligible.

State and explain the effect, if any, of the internal resistance of the new cell on the position of the null point.
